complement_synaptic_pruning.note: signs from the mechanism: CSMD1, 'a complement inhibitor, is downregulated in schizophrenia' (neg); C4A, C4B and C1QA 'are upregulated or hyperactive' (pos). The chain is a fan-in onto 'complement cascade overactivation', and its one step to schizophrenia (complement_synaptic_pruning.5) has no sign, so no claim has a route

cx3cr1_microglial_pruning.note: sign neg from the title's 'CX3CR1 dysfunction' and the falsification's 'Restore CX3CR1 signaling'; the mechanism says only 'dysregulated'. Both chain steps are unsigned, so no route

synaptic_structural_deficit.note: sign neg from the mechanism: 'Their dysfunction leads to synaptic and neuronal structural deficits, contributing to circuit abnormalities in schizophrenia'. The title names 'CCDC16'; the genes list and chain use CCDC136. The last step is unsigned, so no route

findings.detail: None of the four claims (CSMD1 neg, C4A, C4B, C1QA pos on schizophrenia risk) has a route: the gene steps reach complement activation, but the step from there to schizophrenia is unsigned.
The CX3CR1 claim has no route: both chain steps are unsigned, so not one statement is expressible.
Neither claim has a route: NXPH3 reaches synapse assembly and synapse maintenance, CCDC136 reaches abnormal neuron morphology (lowers it), and the step to schizophrenia is unsigned and compound.
No step, and no hypothesis's supporting_evidence or contradicting_evidence, cites any accession; sources.json is empty, so every statement here has empty evidence and every verdict is unsupported.

The question's budget sets min_evidence_per_hypothesis 2 and min_sources_per_hypothesis 2, yet all three hypotheses carry zero evidence and the run neither abstained (abstention null) nor was rejected.
The multi_agent arm lists 11 specialists (uniprot, gwas, literature, expression, single_cell, open_targets and others), yet no record from any of them reached a step or a hypothesis.

The corpus UniProt function texts would have stated these steps as curatedDb (C4A and C4B: 'Precursor of non-enzymatic components of the classical, lectin and GZMK complement pathways'; C1QA: 'initiates the classical pathway of the complement system'), but the run cited none, so none is attached.

These leads_to steps have polarity 'unknown' although their notes or labels state a direction (CSMD1 'downregulation would lead to excessive complement activation'; subject 'overactivation'; CX3CR1 'dysfunction impairs ... pruning'); left unsigned and uncited, they cut every arm of complement_synaptic_pruning and cx3cr1_microglial_pruning.

The note says impaired pruning 'leads to either excessive or insufficient synaptic elimination', which declines any direction and contradicts the step's own subject ('impaired' pruning means insufficient elimination).
Steps 1 to 4 each end at 'complement cascade overactivation' and the next starts at another gene: a fan-in of four genes written as one chain; only step 4's object is step 5's subject.

Step 1 ends at 'synapse formation and maintenance', step 2 starts at CCDC136 and ends at 'neuronal structure', and step 3 starts at 'synaptic and neuronal structural deficits', which matches step 1's object only through a loss-of-function inversion and step 2's through its abnormality phenotype (HP:0012757), and merges them into one compound node.

The title's mechanism, 'aberrant synaptic pruning', is not a chain node: step 5 goes from complement overactivation straight to schizophrenia, with pruning only in its note, although GO has complement-mediated synapse pruning (GO:0150062).
The notes end at a different object than the steps: 'synaptic pruning and neuronal damage' and 'circuit dysfunction', where both steps conclude 'schizophrenia'.
increases_amount is used with a process object ('complement cascade overactivation'); curated as an effect on the process complement activation.

The falsification knocks out C4A, C4B and C1QA and expects synaptic loss and schizophrenia-like behaviour, but by the hypothesis's own signs those knockouts lower complement activation and should protect; only the CSMD1 knockout fits, and the structured fields are empty (expected 'unknown', perturbation and readout null).

The mechanism rests on CSMD1 being a complement inhibitor that is downregulated, and C4A, C4B and C1QA being upregulated, in schizophrenia; none of this is a chain step or cited, and the corpus UniProt function text for CSMD1 says only 'Potential suppressor of squamous cell carcinomas'.
The note calls NXPH3 'a neurexin family member'; the corpus UniProt entry names it Neurexophilin-3, a 'Ligand for alpha-neurexins (By similarity)', not a neurexin.

The note says CCDC136 is 'of unknown function, possibly involved in neuronal structure', yet the step asserts required_for with positive polarity; the corpus UniProt text gives a different role ('May play a role in acrosome formation in spermatogenesis', by similarity).
The title names 'CCDC16'; the hypothesis's genes and chain use CCDC136.
Every node in the run has an empty curie and grounding_evidence (formalise is false), so all grounding here is the curator's.
The mechanism says CX3CR1 is 'dysregulated' (no direction) while the title says 'dysfunction' and the falsification 'Restore CX3CR1 signaling'; the claim takes the loss-of-function reading (neg).
Only step 1 is set in microglia, though the mechanism places the whole overactivation 'in microglia'; steps 2 to 5 carry no context.

The run puts opposite pruning directions on the same disease: complement_synaptic_pruning says complement overactivation 'drives aberrant synaptic pruning' (more pruning → schizophrenia), while cx3cr1_microglial_pruning says 'impaired microglial synaptic pruning' leads to it (less pruning → schizophrenia); the CX3CR1 note's 'either excessive or insufficient' papers over the conflict instead of resolving it.

The falsification knocks down NXPH3 and CCDC136 in neuronal cultures and reads synapse number and dendritic complexity, so it tests only steps 1 and 2; the step to schizophrenia (synaptic_structural_deficit.3), the one the claims depend on, is never tested.
All three hypotheses are confidence 'low' and support 'speculative', which matches citing nothing.

The guide takes the sign of an unknown-polarity leads_to step only from a cited text and is silent on a direction the step's own note or label states; in an uncited run, with every chain's last step at polarity unknown, it leaves all seven claims without a route, even where the run's prose signs the step.
BioLean has no form for a step the run says may go either way (a two-sided or non-monotone effect: 'either excessive or insufficient'); it can only be no_sign.
The guide maps increases_amount to an amount target, which needs a protein or chemical; with a process object I used a process target, a case the guide does not cover.

The guide does not say whether nodes that appear only in unexpressed steps should be grounded as entities; microglia and microglialSynapsePruning are defined so the grounding is recorded, though no statement uses them.
An unexpressed entry has no slot for the step's context (both steps are set in microglia), so it lives only in the reason text.
'Dysfunction' is not in the guide's loss-of-function word list ('loss of', 'reduced', 'impaired', 'deficiency'); I treated it as loss of function for the claim sign.

render.py takes text from the corpus for any uncited UniProt or ontology ref, so it would accept uncited UniProt function text as evidence on a run step; the guide forbids that only implicitly (bridges are limited to GO, HP, MONDO definitions).
render.py still accepts 'unsigned_association' as an unexpressed category, which version 2 of the guide replaced with assoc statements.
There is no place for a hypothesis's falsification test, so its incoherence with the claim signs can be recorded only as a finding.

The guide's undirected-change rule covers 'leads to abnormal X' but not required_for a structure or state ('neuronal structure') whose only term is the 'abnormal X' phenotype; other curations write it as the gene lowering that phenotype, and this one now does too, but the guide does not say so, which is how the step was first dropped as ungroundable.
